correctness.rationale: Nested neighborhoods identify nonempty extreme universal classes on both sides. Necessity follows by dominating minimum-neighborhood vertices; sufficiency follows because one selected universal vertex from each side dominates its opposite bipartition. The same pair connects the entire selected induced subgraph. Independent subset choices give the product polynomial, and algebraic factorization gives the root multiset. Exact exhaustive enumeration checked 671 canonical connected chain graphs and 781140 subsets through total order eleven.

evidence: Chaluvaraju--Chaitra (2014), DOI 10.26713/jims.v6i2.256, treats general properties and several families/operations, including complete bipartite graphs, but its full text contains no chain-graph result.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither the general polynomial paper nor the secure-total-domination chain-graph paper implies the enumeration of all total dominating sets of arbitrary chain graphs. The present theorem uses only the extreme nested neighborhoods and applies uniformly to every connected chain graph.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies every total dominating set of a standard graph class, proves automatic connectivity of all such sets, gives a closed polynomial factorization, exact minimum-set count, full support, complete root multiset, and a real-rootedness criterion. These are natural structural and enumerative consequences rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
